                    A Sample Protocol in RFCXML v3 Text

Abstract

   This document is a synthetic sample used to test the parser against
   the unpaginated text layout produced by xml2rfc version 3.  It has
   a table, nested lists, a definition list, and a figure.

Status of This Memo

   This is an Internet Standards Track document.

Table of Contents

   1.  Introduction
     1.1.  Requirements Language
   2.  Protocol Overview
   3.  Data Types
   4.  IANA Considerations
   5.  References
     5.1.  Normative References
   Appendix A.  Example Exchange
   Authors' Addresses

1.  Introduction

   The Sample Protocol (SP) is a stateless request/response protocol
   that is described here only to exercise the parser.  See Section 2
   for an overview and Appendix A for an example.  It builds on
   [RFC9110] and RFC 2119.

1.1.  Requirements Language

   The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT",
   "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and
   "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in
   BCP 14 [RFC2119] [RFC8174] when, and only when, they appear in all
   capitals, as shown here.

2.  Protocol Overview

   A client sends a request and receives a response:

   *  Requests carry a method and a target.

      -  The method is one of the tokens in Table 1.

      -  The target is a URI reference (Section 4.1 of [RFC3986]).

   *  Responses carry a three-digit status code.

   The following table lists the methods:

   +=========+===========================+===========+
   | Method  | Description               | Reference |
   +=========+===========================+===========+
   | FETCH   | Retrieve a representation | Section 3 |
   +---------+---------------------------+-----------+
   | STORE   | Replace a representation; | Section 3 |
   |         | wraps onto two lines      |           |
   +---------+---------------------------+-----------+

                           Table 1: SP Methods

   Figure 1 shows the message flow.

          +--------+            request            +--------+
          |        | ----------------------------> |        |
          | Client |                               | Server |
          |        | <---------------------------- |        |
          +--------+            response           +--------+

                         Figure 1: Message Flow

3.  Data Types

   Messages are described with the following ABNF:

   message       = start-line CRLF *( header CRLF ) CRLF [ body ]
   start-line    = method SP target SP version
   header        = field-name ":" OWS field-value OWS

   Example request:

   FETCH /items/42 SP/1.0
   Host: example.com
   Accept: application/json

   Field definitions:

   method:  One of FETCH or STORE.  Implementations MUST reject other
      tokens.

   target:  The resource identifier.

   version:  Always "SP/1.0" in this version of the protocol.

4.  IANA Considerations

   This document has no IANA actions.

              RFC 3986, DOI 10.17487/RFC3986, January 2005,

              DOI 10.17487/RFC9110, June 2022,
              <https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9110>.

Appendix A.  Example Exchange

   A complete exchange looks like this:

   {
     "method": "FETCH",
     "target": "/items/42",
     "status": 200
   }
